title: Closure of K-flat complexes
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Bounded-above complexes of flat $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] are K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. The class of K-flat complexes is closed under cones and countable direct sums (and hence under homotopy colimits), and countable direct sums of flat $\mathcal O$-modules are flat.

source.place: Lemma 06YS (K-flatness of bounded-above flat complexes and closure under the homotopy-colimit construction)

proof.text: The bounded-above flat-complex argument of Stacks 06YS applies to the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules: filter the tensor total complex by stupid truncations. Each associated graded piece is a tensor product with one flat term and is acyclic; induction on the upper bound gives acyclicity. Thus every bounded-above complex of flat $\mathcal O$-modules is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site].

source.place: Lemma 06YS, bounded-above flat complexes are K-flat

proof.text: Cones and countable direct sums of K-flat complexes of $\mathcal O$-modules are K-flat by [lem-pc-kflat-cone-direct-sum]. The homotopy colimit of a sequence $E_0^\bullet\to E_1^\bullet\to\cdots$ is by definition the cone of $1-\operatorname{shift}:\bigoplus_nE_n^\bullet\to\bigoplus_nE_n^\bullet$, as in [lem-pc-complex-hocolim-colimit]; if every $E_n^\bullet$ is K-flat, the countable sum $\bigoplus_nE_n^\bullet$ is K-flat and so is the cone of this endomorphism, by the two clauses of [lem-pc-kflat-cone-direct-sum]. Hence the class of K-flat complexes is closed under homotopy colimits.

source.place: Lemma 06YS, closure of K-flat complexes under cones and direct sums

proof.text: Take $\mathcal B=\Mod(\mathcal O)$. It is a Grothendieck abelian category by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] (for $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ to be abelian the site is small or essentially small, and replacing $\mathcal C$ by an equivalent small site changes neither $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ nor $\otimes_{\mathcal O}$), and by [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] the tensor product $\otimes_{\mathcal O}$ makes it symmetric, hence braided, monoidal closed, so $\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}-$ is a left adjoint and right exact for every $\mathcal F$, and $\mathcal G\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal F\cong\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal G$ naturally. A flat $\mathcal O$-module $\mathcal F$ [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] has $-\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal F$, hence $\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}-$, exact, so $\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}-$ preserves finite limits and $\mathcal F$ is flat in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-coproduct]. That theorem applied to a countable family $(\mathcal F_n)_{n\in\mathbf N}$ of flat $\mathcal O$-modules shows that $(\bigoplus_n\mathcal F_n)\otimes_{\mathcal O}-$ preserves finite limits; being also right exact, it is exact, and by the symmetry so is $-\otimes_{\mathcal O}\bigoplus_n\mathcal F_n$. Thus $\bigoplus_n\mathcal F_n$ is flat.
